I am writing this review 20 days after the birth of our baby boy, delivered under the observation of Dr. Ashwini Tambolkar at Laxmi Maternity & Surgical Nursing Home, Kandivali East.

From the very first consultation till the day of discharge, our experience has been nothing less than wonderful. Dr. Ashwini is extremely kind, polite, understanding and supportive. My wife was very anxious about her second pregnancy and the need for a C-section, but under Dr. Ashwini’s guidance, care, and reassurance, the entire process turned into a smooth and happy experience. The Mavshi staff and nursing team deserve special appreciation. No matter the time—day, midnight, or early morning—they were always available, attentive, and caring. Their skills, knowledge, and emotional support helped my wife recover quickly, especially during the first two days of post-delivery pain. They also took wonderful care of our baby, ensuring every little need was met.

Even my mother and mother-in-law expressed their gratitude, saying they had never seen such smooth and caring management of delivery compared to the difficult situations they had witnessed earlier in life.
Spending five days in the hospital felt like being with family. Despite staying one extra day beyond our package, the hospital did not charge us, which shows their genuine concern for patients over profits.

By the time of discharge, a strong bond had formed with the doctor, nurses, and mavshi staff. Even our elder son enjoyed his time there without missing school, thanks to the warmth of the hospital environment.

We are deeply thankful to Dr. Ashwini Tambolkar Ma’am, all the nursing staff, and the support team for giving us such a positive and memorable experience during this special phase of our life.

— Mr. & Mrs. Priyanka Shudhdodhan Ambhore

To make matters worse, I asked the doctor if he could prescribe a medicine to help my father calm down. Instead of writing a prescription, the doctor simply gave me the name of a medication—which obviously cannot be bought over the counter without a prescription. When I asked him to actually write the prescription for it, he flatly refused, claiming he was **"not authorized"** to give one.
What is the point of an emergency doctor who cannot or will not prescribe medication to stabilize a patient in crisis? The service was extremely bad, and the staff's attitude was incredibly dismissive and rude during a highly stressful time for our family.
I would highly advise management to look into the basic qualifications and training of their emergency staff. Absolutely unacceptable and dangerous service.

featured_reviews.review_text:
The care given is really good.
My mother was admitted here. They give personalized attention and good care.
The doctors are well experienced, attentive and explain you everything properly.
The staff is very helpful when it comes to solving any problem.
You are not allowed to get your food. So, if you are a patient's relative, as a local guide I would suggest don't fall for canteen food. The canteen food mostly offers biscuits and stuff like misal pav vada. 1-2 protein bars which are processed.

There is a seperate menu from which you can order food which offers options like Khichadi and dahi which are decent.
Because, when your relatives is admitted in the hospital neglecting your own health and falling for sugary oily food may not be a good option.

I would suggest they have seperate menu, which you will need to call a number and ask for, there you get better options than the processed food.

There is personalised dietician assigned to each patient. She mostly gives balanced options for the patients. I had seen Marie Biscuit in my mom's diet. I personally don't want my mom to eat biscuits with palm oil in it. So, she switched the snack.
So, if you have special preferences. You can always communicate.

One more suggestion to the hospital.
If you have a room patient's relative mostly gets assigned bed.
But if the patient is in the ICU there is no assigned bed for the patient's relative. Which is mostly offered in some other hospitals. So, that could be added.

My sister recently delivered her baby here, and our overall experience was average.

Throughout the pregnancy, we were asked to undergo multiple scans and make several visits. While we understand the importance of regular monitoring, it did feel like some of them may not have been necessary.

The room provided was quite compact and felt a bit suffocating. The beds were small and not very comfortable. My mother stayed with my sister, and the accompanying bed was also quite uncomfortable for her. Additionally, the room did not appear to be maintained as neatly as expected.

One major concern was the mosquito issue, especially during the evening. There were quite a lot of mosquitoes around the building and even inside the room. Unfortunately, the newborn was also bitten by mosquitoes, and my sister was unable to get proper rest post-delivery.
